items.title: Public Preview: Disable VNet peering route
items.description:
Announcing the public preview of disable VNet peering route, a route-table capability that gives you more control over traffic between peered virtual networks. DPR suppresses system-generated peering routes on subnets associated with the route table while preserving the peering connection itself.     

In large hub-and-spoke networks, you can pair this feature with a summarized user-defined route to direct traffic through a network virtual appliance, such as Azure Firewall, instead of maintaining a separate override for every spoke. This helps simplify route management as your network grows.            

Manage DPR through route-table configuration or Azure Virtual Network Manager routing rule collections. You configure the replacement UDRs and inspection path; DPR does not create them automatically.        

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Service tag match condition for Azure Front Door Premium WAF
items.description:
Announcing the general availability of the service tag match condition for Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) custom rules on Azure Front Door Premium. 

Service tags represent groups of IP address prefixes used by Azure services, and Microsoft updates them automatically as addresses change. Custom rules can now match a HTTP request's source IP address against service tags, so you can control traffic from Azure services without building and maintaining lists of IPs.  

With service tag matching, you can: 

  • Allow Azure services your application relies on, such as monitoring and health checks, through to your endpoints. 
  • Block traffic from Azure services your application never expects to receive requests from. 
  • Restrict sensitive paths, such as admin endpoints, by combining a service tag with URI, host, or request method conditions. 
  • Rate limit traffic from an Azure service instead of blocking it outright. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Keyless TLS on Application Gateway with Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
items.description:
Azure Application Gateway now supports keyless TLS termination using certificates whose private keys stay in Azure Key Vault Managed HSM. Each TLS handshake signature is performed inside the HSM, and the private key is never exported to the gateway. 

This integration helps you: 

  • Maintain private key custody within a dedicated HSM boundary. 
  • Use managed identities and role-based access control for key access. 
  • Monitor signing operations through Managed HSM diagnostic logs. 
  • Obtain cryptographic evidence that the TLS key was generated and is stored in a FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated HSM. 
  • Support separation of duties and centralized key management. 

Learn more: 

  • What is keyless TLS for Azure Application Gateway and Azure Key Vault Managed HSM? 
  • Tutorial: Configure keyless TLS termination with Azure Key Vault Managed HSM 
  • What is Azure Key Vault Managed HSM?

items.title: Generally Available: Advanced platform metrics for Azure Monitor
items.description:
Advanced platform metrics for Azure Monitor are now generally available. Advanced platform metrics provide finer-grained signals that help customers more quickly and accurately identify changes and trends within their resources.

With this release, customers can enable advanced platform metrics directly from the Azure portal, with an in-product banner prompting enablement for subscriptions where the feature is not yet enabled. Advanced platform metrics are also now available in Fairfax and Mooncake, expanding availability beyond the public cloud.
